previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease, diabetes, and heart failure was admitted for a deceased donor pediatric en bloc kidney transplant. The surgery was complicated by significant scarring, intraoperative oozing requiring platelet transfusion, and the incidental finding of a nodular liver leading to a biopsy that revealed stage IV fibrosis. Postoperatively, he developed slow graft function, which resolved as creatinine improved from 8.4 to 1.2 and urine output increased. He experienced volume overload and atrial tachycardia, managed with diuresis and rate control, with plans for outpatient rhythm evaluation. Ascites developed, and a paracentesis revealed Candida krusei peritonitis, treated with micafungin via a newly placed PICC line. A surgical wound leak necessitated placement of a wound VAC. Hyperglycemia from steroid use required insulin initiation. He was discharged home with home health support, on immunosuppression, antifungal therapy, and wound care, with stable graft function and resolved complications.

radiology_notes.text:
EXAM:  Renal transplant ultrasound.

CLINICAL INFORMATION:  Pain over transplant site.  No bowel movement for three
days.

___ as well as ___.

FINDINGS:  Grayscale and color and spectral Doppler sonographic evaluation of
the transplanted kidneys and bladder were obtained.  Patient had two
transplanted pediatric kidneys in the right lower quadrant.  The numbering of
the kidneys is reversed from previous.  On the images, transplant kidney #1
corresponds to previously described transplant kidney #2 and transplant kidney
#2 labeled on the study previously referred to transplant kidney #1.  The
superior more transplant kidney today measures 8.4 cm in length and the
inferior more measures 8.1 cm in length.  Both kidneys demonstrate increased
pelvic fullness/dilatation compared to the prior study.

Transplant kidney labeled #2 in this study, but previously labelled #1
demonstrates resistive indices in the upper pole was 0.84, in the mid pole,
0.80 and in the lower pole, 0.78 (previous range of 0.74-0.84).  Good
diastolic flow is seen.  The resistive indices in the kidney labeled #1 on
this study, but previously would be #2 on the prior studies, in the upper pole
was 0.81, mid pole, 0.81, and lower pole, 0.77 (previously ranged from
0.73-0.78).  The renal veins are patent.  The bladder is not fully distended,
but linear echogenic foci likely correspond to ureteral stents seen on
abdominal radiograph performed later the same date.  There may be a small
amount of free fluid adjacent to the urinary bladder.  There is a large
complex perinephric collection.  As seen previously, exact size is difficult
to compare due to differences in sonographer and technique, however, likely
stable to possibly minimally increased, and today measures up to 13.9 x 6.6 x
7.1 cm.

IMPRESSION:
1.  Two right lower quadrant transplanted pediatric kidneys with resistive
indices as above and good diastolic flow throughout.

2.  Interval increase in pelvic fullness/dilatation of both kidneys.

3.  Large complex perinephric fluid collection again seen.

EXAM:  Abdomen, supine and upright views.

CLINICAL INDICATION:  Pain over transplant site.  No bowel movement for three
days.

___.

FINDINGS:  Supine and upright views of the abdomen were obtained.  There is a
non-obstructive bowel gas pattern.  No large air-fluid levels are seen.  There
is no evidence of free air.  Two single pigtail catheter/stents are seen
projecting over the pelvis and extending to the right, which may represent
ureteral stents.  Battery pack is seen projecting over the epigastrium. 
Pelvic phleboliths are seen.  Pelvic vascular calcifications are seen.

IMPRESSION:  No evidence of bowel obstruction.  Moderate colonic fecal
loading.

CHEST RADIOGRAPH

INDICATION:  Pre-existing PICC line, evaluation.

COMPARISON:  ___.

FINDINGS:  As compared to the previous radiograph, the right internal jugular
vein catheter has been removed.  The patient has a PICC line on the left. The
course of the line is unremarkable, the tip of the line projects over the
upper-to-mid SVC.  There is no evidence of complications, notably no
pneumothorax.  No pleural effusions.  External pacemaker projecting over the
upper quadrant.  Moderate cardiomegaly.  No pulmonary edema.  No pneumonia.
